claims.claim: The Museum of Pop Culture records that Mohan came to TSR in 1979 from newspaper work, having been a reporter and then a sports and state editor.
claims.source: Museum of Pop Culture, Science Fiction and Fantasy Hall of Fame inductee page, 2025
claims.quote: as a reporter for the Lake Geneva Regional News

claims.claim: Vallese describes the RPG editor's job as extending past words and game stats to structure, plot, playability and how the text would fit the layout.
claims.source: Ray Vallese, TSR Planescape editor, interviewed at Exposition Break, 2022
claims.quote: issues like structure, plot, playability, how things would fit
claims.page: answer on what an RPG editor does

claims.claim: Vallese names Michele Carter as the other primary Planescape editor of that era.
claims.source: Ray Vallese, TSR Planescape editor, interviewed at Exposition Break, 2022
claims.quote: The other primary Planescape editor of that era was Michele

claims.claim: The DUNGEON staff give 500 words as the rough average word count of a single published encounter.
claims.source: The DUNGEON Staff, DUNGEON Submission Guidelines, Appendix II: Adventure Design Guide
claims.quote: a rough average for a single encounter’s word count

claims.claim: The DUNGEON staff cap a sidebar at 300 words and ask writers to keep the number of sidebars to a minimum.
claims.source: The DUNGEON Staff, DUNGEON Submission Guidelines, Appendix II: Adventure Design Guide
claims.quote: sidebars in your adventure to a minimum, and to no

claims.claim: The DUNGEON guidelines require an author bio of 25 words at the end of an adventure or backdrop manuscript.
claims.source: The DUNGEON Staff, DUNGEON Submission Guidelines, The Manuscript

claims.claim: The Dragon guidelines state that a full page of text in the magazine contains about 750 words.
claims.source: Dragon Writers Guidelines (Dragon editorial staff), Format and Style
claims.quote: A full page of text in Dragon contains about 750 words.

claims.claim: Sims calls absolutist statements editorial nightmares because they paint later creation in a shared setting into a corner.
claims.source: Chris S. Sims, Writing: Generalizations and Absolutes, 2020
claims.quote: Absolutist statements are, instead, editorial nightmares.

claims.claim: Sims names the flat-culture issue: imaginary peoples written as homogeneous, which he says even Eberron's reimagining fails to escape.
claims.source: Chris S. Sims, Writing: Generalizations and Absolutes, 2020
claims.quote: I call this problem the “flat-culture issue.”

claims.claim: Perkins says the Planescape cant is mostly absent from Warriors of Heaven, apart from an occasional slang word he slipped past the editors.
claims.source: Christopher Perkins, interviewed at Planescape: I am the Mimir, 1999

claims.claim: Winter says that at TSR the editor took the manuscript over from the designer and managed everything about it thereafter, including development, layout, art orders and proofreading.
claims.source: Steve Winter, TSR editor, interviewed at Grognardia, 2009
claims.quote: an editor took over and managed everything about the manuscript

verdicts.trueWording: as a reporter for the Lake Geneva Regional News
verdicts.note: Live mopop.org fetched 200 (raw HTML, curl, browser UA). Inductee bio body: begins career as reporter there, then Beloit Daily News as sports editor and then state editor, 'before joining TSR in 1979'. Every limb supported. Page header confirms 'Kim Mohan | SFFHOF Inductee', 'Induction Year 2025'.

verdicts.trueWording: issues like structure, plot, playability, how things would fit
verdicts.note: Live expositionbreak.com fetched 200 (raw HTML). In Ray Vallese's answer to the question on what an RPG editor does: his job was editing the words and game stats but also considering larger issues of that list, plus fitting in the layout. All limbs supported; attribution to Vallese correct.

verdicts.trueWording: The other primary Planescape editor of that era was Michele
verdicts.note: Same raw page, same fetch. Parenthetical inside Ray Vallese's answer on how roles were decided; continues 'Carter, who deserves just as much credit as any of us.' Named by Vallese, as claimed.

verdicts.trueWording: a rough average for a single encounter's word count
verdicts.note: PDF fetched 200 and text-extracted with pdftotext -layout (6 pages). Quote is the parenthetical in the APPENDIX II bullet telling writers to multiply encounter count by 500. Section matches. Nuance not contradicting the claim: the same bullet adds that higher-level encounter areas run wordier, averaging 750 or 1,000.

verdicts.trueWording: sidebars in your adventure to a minimum, and to no
verdicts.note: Same PDF text. APPENDIX II bullet: keep the number of sidebars to a minimum and to no more than 300 words in length. Both limbs (the 300-word cap and the minimise instruction) supported in one sentence. Later sections repeat the 300-word cap for the Scaling and Adapting sidebars.

Same PDF text. Section 'The Manuscript', numbered rule 4, exactly as cited: at the end of your manuscript write it, with the parenthetical restricting it to adventure and backdrop manuscript submissions. All limbs supported; page calls it a personal bio, and Appendix II has a matching mandatory Author Bio section.

verdicts.trueWording: A full page of text in Dragon contains about 750 words.
verdicts.note: Live paizo.com/writersguidelines/dragon.html fetched 200 (raw HTML). Sentence stands alone under the 'Format and Style' heading, exactly as cited. Eleven words, within the twelve-word cap.

verdicts.trueWording: Absolutist statements are, instead, editorial nightmares.
verdicts.note: Live chrisssims.wordpress.com fetched 200 (raw HTML). Closing sentence of a paragraph under 'Superlatives or Absolutisms'; the same paragraph supplies the causal limb, saying that in a shared universe of fiction or game design an absolute statement paints further creation into a corner.

verdicts.trueWording: I call this problem the “flat-culture issue.”
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Under the 'Generalizations' heading; the preceding clause names the problem as homogeny among imaginary people, and the next sentences credit Eberron's sophisticated takes but say it fails to escape the flat-culture issue with much of its reimagining. Every limb supported.

Live mimir.net fetched 200 (raw HTML). Perkins's answer on how the product is written: Warriors of Heaven is a core AD&D product not embracing most Planescape products' narrative style; the quoted clause continues that he slipped the occasional 'basher' and 'leatherhead' past the editors. Both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: an editor took over and managed everything about the manuscript
verdicts.note: Live grognardia.blogspot.com fetched 200 (raw HTML). Winter's answer to question 4 on editing at TSR: the designer wrote the original manuscript, then this, 'from that point on' with the parenthetical listing additional development, editing, layout, ordering art and maps, proofreading and typefitting. Every limb supported.
